name: _sparse_csr_tensor_unsafe
description: Representative ATen signature (not an exclusive ABI), copied verbatim from the supplied schema: aten::_sparse_csr_tensor_unsafe(Tensor crow_indices, Tensor col_indices, Tensor values, int[] size, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Layout? layout=None, Device? device=None, bool? pin_memory=None) -> Tensor. All supplied registered schema strings, verbatim: aten::_sparse_csr_tensor_unsafe(Tensor crow_indices, Tensor col_indices, Tensor values, int[] size, *, ScalarType? dtype=None, Layout? layout=None, Device? device=None, bool? pin_memory=None) -> Tensor. The ATen defaults for dtype/layout/device/pin_memory are the C++ 'None' sentinels (non-JSON scalar/list/device values), rendered here as the stable JSON null; they are preserved as omitted-argument sentinels, not as invented concrete defaults. The original Gems pytest owns the full overload, keyword-argument, return, error, mutation and alias contract; this definition records one representative signature and must never be used to narrow, delete or adapt tests, workloads or reference behavior to this single form. Semantics derived from the tests: this unsafe compressed-sparse-row factory builds a sparse_csr tensor from three component tensors plus an int-list `size` argument (the pytest passes a Python list, and in one case a tuple; no Tensor- or torch.Size-typed size form is exercised), storing the caller's components by reference and copying nothing (no metadata validation, no compaction, no re-indexing). The returned tensor reports layout sparse_csr, the requested size/shape, sparse_dim()/dense_dim()/numel()/_nnz() matching the native oracle, and exposes crow_indices(), col_indices() and values() as new wrappers over the caller's own storage, preserving each component's storage offset, stride, shape, dtype and device; writes through the caller's buffer are visible in the stored component and the three components remain three independent buffers. Because metadata is unchecked, the factory accepts descriptors with short or over-long row pointers, out-of-range or unsorted column indices, more stored entries than the last row pointer reports, non-integer index dtypes, and rank-0/rank-1 size values; size may be passed as a list or as a tuple. The pytest's only oracle is torch.ops.aten._sparse_csr_tensor_unsafe, so it establishes nothing about what a checked sparse_csr_tensor builder would reject. dtype defaults to float32 when omitted and must equal the values dtype when supplied (otherwise RuntimeError); the index dtype is kept verbatim. Rank >= 2 sizes express two trailing matrix extents plus optional leading batch extents, where each batch entry owns its own row-pointer block and the leading extent is reflected in sparse_dim(); dense-dim (value-block) shapes are expressed by higher-rank values. The operator rejects non-CSR layouts (sparse_bsr, sparse_csc, strided), mismatched dtype, negative sizes, non-tensor components, cross-device components and pin_memory=True together with accelerator components, all via RuntimeError. The result neither requires grad nor has a grad_fn even when the stored values require grad (no autograd edge, alias-only factory). These keyword/default/error/alias behaviors live in the pytest and are only summarized here; no conditional-effect modeling is implied.
